stories.blurb: A new starter copies the headache that sent Clara home, just as the Friday on-call rota goes up.

opener.setting: Wednesday, 15:30, the team room at Halden. The Friday on-call rota has just gone up on the shared screen.

lines.text: “Clara, go home. Now. I'll take the release notes, you've done plenty.”
lines.cue: pulling her chair out, already reaching for her laptop

opener.ask: Can you spot a trap being copied in this team room, and choose a move that stops it rather than feeds it?

items.text: “Go home. Now. I'll take the release notes, you've done plenty.”
items.cue: Clara has both hands pressed to her temples. Daniel is already pulling her chair out.
options: A cold nod, for doing wrong
A big warm nod, for being
Nothing, she was not noticed
items.why: Daniel dropped everything the second Clara winced, and he offered to take her work too. She got the nod for being unwell. She had done nothing to earn it.

traps.0: A cold nod would sound like “We're all tired, Clara.” Daniel did the opposite, and fast.
traps.2: Nothing would mean Clara sat there with her head in her hands unseen. Daniel was out of his chair before she finished speaking.

items.example:
A school office, a teacher to a girl who goes pale in assembly: “Sit down, love, I'll ring your mum.”
The girl is fussed over, and the register is forgotten for the morning.

items.cue: eyes on the Friday on-call rota that has just popped up on the shared screen, voice pitched exactly like Clara's
options: A real headache, nothing else
A plain protest about the Friday rota
A copy of what worked for Clara
items.why: The rota is part of it, but the timing and the words say more. Same complaint, same moment, same reward: Callum watched the headache work for Clara, and he is trying it on.

traps.0: A real headache would turn up by itself. This one arrived ten minutes after Clara's, the instant his name appeared against Friday night.
traps.1: A protest about the rota would be loud and plain, like “I can't do Friday.” Callum is asking for the nod, and the rota hardly comes into it.

items.example:
A family wedding, a cousin who suddenly needs the loo when the washing-up starts. Last time an aunt left the room in a fuss and got her tea brought to her.
The timing gives the copy away.

options: Jess found a move that works

Omar is cross with the recruiters
items.why: Jess found that a dead laptop got her out of the demo, so she kept using it, and nobody had to decide it was a lie. Callum is the second person on this team to find the same exit.

traps.1: Real bad luck does not land on the same day every month. Omar is describing a pattern he has seen before.
traps.2: His tone is tired, not angry at the people who hired her. The line is about a pattern that works on him.

items.title: Wednesday, 15:40, the team room at Halden
items.setting: Ten minutes after Clara went home with Daniel's blessing. The Friday rota is still on the screen, and Callum is watching Daniel the way a goalkeeper watches a penalty taker.

beats.cue: one hand on his forehead, eyes on the rota

lines.text: “Poor Callum. Daniel, take him off Friday night, he looks wrecked.”
lines.outcome: Daniel nods before you finish. Callum's name is rubbed off the rota, and he sits straighter than a person with a pounding head should.
lines.why: You fed the bid. It got him what he wanted, so next time he will try it sooner and louder. A trap move ends the scene here.

lines.text: “Is it the head, or is it Friday night on-call?” (said low, with a half smile)
lines.outcome: Callum snorts. “Friday night on-call.” Omar coughs into his mug to hide a laugh. The bid never gets going.
lines.why: You caught the bid with a joke that lets him off, and nobody had to be the villain. The trap is broken while it is still being born.

lines.text: “He just doesn't want to do the rota, Daniel.”
lines.outcome: Callum glares at you. Daniel frowns, then offers him a glass of water anyway, to keep the peace.
lines.why: The trap stops, but by shaming. It works for today and teaches him to hide the next bid better, so it is the wrong tool.

beats.text: “Daniel, could I work from home tomorrow? Head's bad. And Friday could go to someone else, probably.”
beats.cue: a sly look, seeing how far this will go

lines.text: “Ring in if you need a day, mate. It's fine.”
lines.outcome: Callum nods and says nothing. The rota is still empty next to Friday. He knows it works.
lines.why: Giving in is gentle and does no harm today. The honest answer is still missing.

lines.text: “Daniel, send him home, he's clearly ill.”
lines.outcome: Daniel agrees. Callum shuts his laptop with a small, pleased click, and the next bid is already forming.
lines.why: You took the bid at face value and rewarded it. Feeding the copy is the same move as feeding the original, and it ends the scene early.

lines.text: “Which is it, the head or Friday? Tell me straight and I'll back you on either.”
lines.outcome: He holds out for a second, then laughs. “Friday. I've never done on-call.” Omar says he will sit with him for the first hour.
lines.why: You asked for the real answer, and that let him be honest without losing face. A kind question gives a person a way out of the bid.

beats.text: “What's going on with Callum's head? Clara went down like a stone an hour ago.”
beats.cue: turning from the screen, pen tapping

lines.text: “His head's fine, Daniel. He's copying Clara.”
lines.outcome: Daniel's face closes. “He's three weeks in. Don't say that.” The room gets cold for a moment.
lines.why: Naming the copy is true, but it lands on Daniel's care, so he defends Callum and the copying gets an audience.

lines.text: “It's been a long three weeks for him, Daniel. Shall we ask what he needs for Friday?”
lines.outcome: Daniel stops tapping. “Ask him?” He looks at Callum, who has no answer ready.
lines.why: You moved from guessing to asking. That leaves Callum a real choice, and the trap loses its audience.

items.payoff: Daniel moves Callum's on-call to Omar, who sighs and says nothing. The trap has set one notch, and Omar notices.

items.title: Wednesday, 16:20, the Halden kitchenette
items.setting: Omar is rinsing the same mug for the third time. Callum has gone to the loo, and his laptop is still open on the release checklist.

beats.text: “Jess did exactly this. A dead laptop on every demo day. I never knew whether to believe her.”
beats.cue: rinsing the mug, not looking at you

lines.text: “You should call his bluff, Omar.”
lines.outcome: Omar nods without looking up. He has heard that from everybody, and it never helped.
lines.why: Nobody asked for advice. It makes you the one who fixes his problem and leaves him nothing to do but agree.

lines.text: “It's hard to tell a real one from the move. Clara got looked after for hers. He's copying what works.”
lines.outcome: Omar stops rinsing. “...Right. He is, isn't he.”
lines.why: You named the pattern without blaming Callum. Copying what works is how a trap spreads, and saying it aloud lets a colleague see it from outside.

lines.text: “That must wear you out.”
lines.outcome: Omar sighs. “It does, a bit.” The moment stays heavy and nothing moves.
lines.why: Warm, but it stays on the feeling and never helps him see the pattern. It is kind, and it opens nothing up.

beats.text: “So what do I do? Put him on the rota anyway, or give him the day?”
beats.cue: a real question this time, no dryness

lines.text: “I'd just believe him, Omar. Easier all round.”
lines.outcome: Omar relaxes. The checklist stays half done, and a headache is now how the day ends.
lines.why: You agreed to let the headache count. That is a trap move, and it ends the scene here with the result below.

lines.text: “Put him on every Friday, no exceptions.”
lines.outcome: “Tried that with Jess,” he says flatly.
lines.why: A rule enforced hard feels like a fight, and the bid keeps its audience. It does no harm, and it still falls short of the best move.

lines.text: “Tell him kindly the headache didn't change the rota, then ask what would help him get ready for Friday.”
lines.outcome: Omar laughs. “That's new. I might try it.”
lines.why: You gave him a plain line that does not shame Callum and does not rescue him. He keeps his dignity, and the bid loses its reward.

beats.text: “Omar, leave the lad alone. Three weeks in, that's all he is.”
beats.cue: from the door, laptop under his arm

lines.text: “You're right, Daniel. Sorry, Omar, I shouldn't have said it.”
lines.outcome: Daniel nods, satisfied. Omar looks at the floor.
lines.why: You gave up the point to keep the peace. It is pleasant, and it leaves the trap running.

lines.text: “He is new, Daniel. That's why he's picking things up so fast.”
lines.outcome: Daniel stops in the doorway, a little startled. “...Hm. Picking things up. Yes.”
lines.why: You agreed he is new and kept the lesson in view. The line protects Callum without pretending the pattern is not there.

items.payoff: Omar believes the headache every Friday from then on, and the bid goes up in price.

lines.outcome: Maya relaxes. The pan stays on the hob, and a bad back is now how the evening ends.
lines.why: You agreed to let the bad back count. That is a trap move, and it ends the scene here with the result below.

beats.text: “Maya, leave him be. He's only sixteen and he's on holiday.”
beats.cue: without turning round, tea towel over one shoulder

lines.text: “He is sixteen, Sam. That's why he's learning it so fast.”
lines.outcome: Sam turns round, a little startled. “...Hm. Learning. Yes.”
lines.why: You agreed he is young and kept the lesson in view. The line protects Josh without pretending the pattern is not there.

lines.text: “Yes, Sam, you're right, I shouldn't have said it.”
lines.outcome: Sam nods, satisfied. Maya looks at the floor.
lines.why: You gave up the point to keep the peace. It is pleasant, and it leaves the trap running.

items.payoff: Maya believes the bad back every night from now on, and the bid goes up in price.

items.who: Josh, on the sofa bed, after the kitchen
items.text: “Ella got the bins done for her. Beth got off cooking. So my back works best on Thursdays.”
items.cue: working it out half aloud, very pleased with himself
options: The Kid's own pilot
The Kid's raw feelings
The Kid's copy of a grown-up rule
items.why: Josh is running a small, clever pilot of his own. He has watched which move gets a nod from the people around him and worked out when it pays. That quick, intuitive thinking sits inside the Kid, and it is where a trap is first set up.

traps.1: Raw feelings would be the groan or the giggle itself, wanting with no plan behind it. Josh is lining up Ella and Beth as evidence, and that is thinking.
traps.2: A copied grown-up rule would sound like something Sam says: “Always do your share.” Josh is not repeating anyone's rule. He is comparing what worked for other people and drawing his own conclusion.

items.example:
A kids' football match in the car park, a boy who has worked out that the other side lets him restart whenever he sulks: “Every time I cry, they give me another go.”
Working out what gets the nod is a plan the child has made.
